question.problem: If the path $C$ is the line segment $\overset{―}{MN}$ traversed from the point $M(1,1)$ to the point $N(3,3),$ then ${\int }_{C}\frac{1}{y}\,dx+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,dy=$
question.worked_solution:
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=i+j$ and $b=3\,i+3\,j.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\  & =i+j+t(3\,i+3\,j-(i+j)) \\  & =i+j+t(2\,i+2\,j) \\  & =(2t+1)\,i+(2t+1)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x(t)=2t+1$ and $y(t)=2t+1$ along the segment.

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=2\,i+2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\frac{1}{y}\,dx+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{y}\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{y}\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{2t+1}\cdot 2+\frac{1}{(2t+1)^{2}}\cdot 2\,dt \\  & ={[\operatorname{ln}⁡(2t+1)-\frac{1}{2t+1}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\cdot 1+1)-\frac{1}{2\cdot 1+1}]-[\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\cdot 0+1)-\frac{1}{2\cdot 0+1}] \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\frac{1}{3}+1 \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3+\frac{2}{3} \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{ln}⁡3+2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
